an5.26:1.1: BB follows the comm in translating ayatana as base (=cause=karana). But the “ayatana” doesn’t “cause” liberation, it is an opportunity for it. The root of ayatana means an extended or stretched out space, i.e. field, region, scope. Here it refers to the “occasion” or “opportunity” within which liberation can happen. Notice how the text uses the locative yattha, tranls. by BB as instrumental “by means of which”. Sure, there’s plenty of places where that works. But here there’s no need.
an5.26:2.3: BB understands yathā yathā … tathā tathā as indicating specificity. But I don’t understand how that works: how do you experience joy in the same way that something is taught? Instead I take it in a distributive sense.
an5.26:2.4: This passage (also at [dn33:2.1.130]() and [dn34:1.6.80]()) contains a key insight into the terms _atthappaṭisaṁvedī_ and _dhammapaṭisaṁvedī_. This also applies to the related terms _atthaveda_ and _dhammaveda_ ([mn7:8.1](), [an6.10:2.6]()), which are essentially the same pair of words, the longer form referring to “one who has _atthaveda_ and _dhammaveda_”. The commentary explains them as the joy of hearing the commentary (_attha_) and text (_dhamma_). Though the mention of the commentary is obviously anachronistic, most translators follow this and render as “inspiration” or similar. However, there is little or no support for this sense of _veda_. It usually means “knowing, experiencing, understanding”, and the commentarial sense of “joy” is not recorded for Sanskrit. This passage says that joy arises for one who has _atthaveda_ and _dhammaveda_. This makes good sense if we take _veda_ in its normal sense of “knowing”, which is what causes joy. This is supported by the earliest gloss on this passage in the late canonical [pe8:297.2](), which says that _atthappaṭisaṁvedī_ and _dhammapaṭisaṁvedī_ are respectively the condition and the cause for examination of the teaching by the mind; there is no mention of “joy”. Now, to examine the teaching, it is essential to know that teaching; while joy is desirable, it is not strictly speaking a necessary condition for examination. Thus both the Sutta usage and oldest commentary support the sense “knowing”.
an5.26:6.3: The commentary explains “that Dhamma” here as the text on meditation methods (_kammaṭṭhānapāḷidhamme_).
